questions.question: Which two organizations conducted the 2001 cooperative CSP pilot study in the Platte River Basin?
required_facts: The cooperative pilot study involved the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).
The other organization was the Nebraska Platte River Cooperative Hydrology Study (COHYST).
forbidden_claims: The pilot study was conducted by NOAA
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against fs11503.pdf physical page 1, Introduction.

questions.question: What kind of acoustic signal does the continuous seismic profiling system generate?
required_facts: The CSP system generates a linear swept, frequency-modulated acoustic signal.
forbidden_claims: The CSP system generates only a single fixed-frequency pulse
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against fs11503.pdf physical page 3 in the CSP system description.

questions.question: What fixed geophone spread was used for the Presidio seismic-refraction lines?
required_facts: The geophones were spaced 6 ft apart.
forbidden_claims: The fixed spread used 24 geophones at 3 m spacing
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against OF12-1191.pdf physical page 8 in Seismic Refraction Survey Data Acquisition.

questions.question: In the Presidio appendix, what does the slope of a traveltime curve represent?
required_facts: The slope represents the apparent velocity of the energy arrival.
forbidden_claims: The slope represents only the geophone spacing
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against OF12-1191.pdf physical page 19 in the appendix description of traveltime curves.

questions.question: Which signal-processor filter range gave the best combination of resolution and penetration for the New River survey, and what limitation remained?
required_facts: The 400 to 1,200 hertz range I setting gave the best combination of resolution and penetration.
It produced very little improvement where soft sediment caused central-channel signal attenuation.
forbidden_claims: The filter setting solved the central-channel attenuation problem
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against report.pdf physical page 16; the limitation is stated immediately after the filter-range conclusion.

questions.question: What average sediment velocity was selected for time-to-depth conversion of the New River seismic reflection records?
required_facts: An average sediment velocity of 6,000 ft/s was selected.
forbidden_claims: The selected time-to-depth velocity was 5,000 ft/s
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against report.pdf physical page 21 in the time-to-depth conversion discussion.

questions.question: For the San Fernando SH survey example, what source and geophone array were used?
required_facts: The source was a 4.0-kg sledgehammer striking a 15.2-cm-wide shear timber with metal endplates.
The array used 24 14-Hz single-component geophones at 3 m spacing.
forbidden_claims: The San Fernando example used a 96-geophone 6-ft spread
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against s10950-021-10042-z.pdf physical page 7 in the San Fernando field-data description.

questions.question: What assumptions underlie the seismic-refraction interpretation formulas in the hydrologic-studies text?
required_facts: Layer boundaries are horizontal or dip at a constant angle, with no land-surface relief.
Each layer is homogeneous and isotropic, and seismic velocity increases with depth.
forbidden_claims: The formulas assume arbitrary topographic relief and decreasing velocity with depth
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked against twri_2-d2.pdf physical page 13 in the assumptions immediately before the two-layer formulas.

questions.question: Under a paper-only filter, what signal-processor filter range gave the best resolution and penetration for the New River survey?
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked the manifest and report.pdf physical page 16: the target evidence belongs to geo-report-1989-4195 with document_type report, excluded by paper-only filtering.

questions.question: Which named regulation required seismic crews to wait exactly 72 hours before beginning a survey?
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manual review of the six controlled PDFs found no named regulation with a 72-hour pre-survey requirement.
